title: Records and local bands he listened to
summary: He heard the Rhythm Kings, Bayersdorffer and Sharkey on record and hired Pinky Vidacovich's band for dances at his house.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Oh, just about all of them. All the local bands, you know. At that time the Rhythm Kings were quite popular when I first started, and Johnny Beisdorfer, and Sharky, a lot of the colored bands I used to listen to. In fact we used to have dance parties at my house, my older brothers had a club and I used to give a dance every so often and hire one of the different bands, Pinky, Pinky Vodakovich at the time, one of the colored bands, different bands you know.
What was the name of the band Pinky was with?

Well it was Pinky and his melody boys. And they really played Dixieland those days, but they didn't call it Dixieland, they just called it jazz. But it was the same type of thing that we play now. But it wasn't quite, it was only music New Orleans people knew, it was that type. That's all they heard. Everybody played the same thing.
